correctness.rationale: Forward arcs use only outdegrees in A and indegrees in B, and the two disjoint reverse arcs use the opposite degree slots; adding a reverse arc therefore cannot create a degree conflict. The only possible cycle alternates the two reversed arcs with the two cross arcs. In the absence of either cross arc, adjoining r₁ to any face is valid, so the full complex is literally a cone. With both cross arcs, deletion Q of r₁ is a cone on r₂, and the link L of r₁ is exactly the subcomplex of Q avoiding the face σ={r₂,x,y}. A further arc sharing one of the distinguished vertices uses a forward slot already occupied by x or y. All remaining choices are precisely matchings on the induced residual graph, so lk_Q(σ)=K. For finite simplicial subcomplexes collapsing the attached cone on L identifies the homotopy type of X with Q/L, which is (Δ²*K)/(∂Δ²*K). This is the homotopy cofiber of a subcomplex in a contractible space, hence Σ(S¹*K)≃Σ³K. For K={∅} the actual quotient is Δ²/∂Δ²=S². The displayed integral shift applies in the cross-complete case, and Jonsson's K₅,₅ computation then gives degree-five Z/3 for K₇,₇. The argument proves homotopy equivalence after suspension, not recoverability of unsuspended homotopy information.
residual_risks: The degree shift is conditional on having both cross edges; without that hypothesis only the cone conclusion holds.
The finite mod-2 diagnostics cannot certify integral torsion; that follows from the homotopy proof and the cited integral residual computation.
